findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects, synced last week." vs. the list below shows only 3 items
findings.fix: Either add a fourth project to the list or change "4 projects" to "3 projects".
findings.violation: The text states 4 projects but only 3 projects are listed in the ul element.

findings.fix: Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` to the head section.
findings.violation: The document lacks a viewport meta tag, which is essential for responsive design and proper scaling on mobile devices.

findings.evidence: `<button id="project-settings-duplicate-btn" type="button" aria-label="Duplicate project"></button>` with no visible content or child elements
findings.fix: Add an icon or visible text inside the button (e.g., `<button id="project-settings-duplicate-btn" type="button" aria-label="Duplicate project">⋮</button>` or similar).
findings.violation: The button is empty with no visible text or icon, relying only on aria-label for accessibility, making it unclear to sighted users.

findings.evidence: `<select id="notification-settings-digest-input">` with three `<option>` elements, none marked as selected
findings.fix: Add `selected` attribute to the first option or whichever should be the default: `<option selected>Daily</option>`.
findings.violation: The select element has no default selected option, so the field appears empty when the form loads.

findings.fix: Replace with `<button id="archive-confirm-archive-btn" type="button">Archive</button>` (with appropriate form structure or JavaScript handler).
findings.violation: A destructive action (archiving a project) is implemented as an anchor link rather than a button, which violates semantic HTML conventions and could bypass form validation or confirmation mechanisms.

findings.evidence: Form contains `` followed by a separate `Continue`
findings.fix: Either make "Continue" the form's submit button and remove "Save", or remove "Continue" and let form submission navigate to the next step via JavaScript.
findings.violation: The form flow is unclear - users must submit the form with "Save" but then separately click "Continue" to proceed, which breaks the expected form submission pattern.
